issues.description: Constructor mismatch for class 'Developer': the problem statement and the template require an initializer with signature init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?) (i.e., two parameters: name and optional monthsOfSwiftExperience). The solution implementation defines init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?, age: Int) (an extra 'age' parameter). Additionally, the solution's Client.swift still calls the two-argument initializer (Developer(name:..., monthsOfSwiftExperience:...)), so the solution repository is internally inconsistent. This discrepancy will cause compilation errors and confuse students about which constructor they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Developer initializer signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: remove the extra 'age: Int' parameter from solution_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift so the initializer matches the problem statement and template as init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?). Ensure the initializer prints the result of swiftExperienceDescription() as required by the exercise and update any call sites if needed. Alternatively, if the 'age' parameter is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement, template, and all call sites (e.g., Client.swift) to document and use init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?, age: Int) consistently.
